purpose: Inspect record boundaries and observable contract evidence for disputed CIR/EIR instances. This audit does not invent a new schema or substitute presence in a report for contract conformance.
method: Use the existing source/evidence record structure and explicit schema-authority references present in repository documents.
Distinguish a dedicated record file from an ID section embedded in a batch, resolution, extraction, or completion report.
Mark field-level contract conformance as unverified where no authoritative machine-readable contract is available in the reviewed material.
Do not promote candidates, adjudicate lifecycle conflicts, or alter canonical registries.

source_contract_audit.boundary: source section plus embedded OBSU-000026 and registry-update assertions
findings: The file labels the source Accepted, Full-Text and includes bibliographic identity fields.
The same file embeds an observation and prescriptive CIR/EIR/KOM update instructions; these are not themselves proof of an authorized registry decision.
source_contract_audit.required_follow_up: Owner confirms source inclusion and separates/links observation and registry decision artifacts.

source_contract_audit.boundary: source subsection embedded in mixed-purpose P2.2/P2.3 completion report
findings: The report provides identifiable bibliographic metadata but combines two sources, multiple observations, EV-000012, and roadmap closure claims.
No evidence in this audit establishes that the source subsection satisfies the complete controlling source contract.
source_contract_audit.required_follow_up: Review SRC-000018 independently against the actual controlling source contract and decide whether to materialize a dedicated record.

source_contract_audit.required_follow_up: Review SRC-000019 independently against the actual controlling source contract and decide whether to materialize a dedicated record.

cross_cutting_findings: EV-BATCH-001.md explicitly names ERS-001 as the schema authority and describes it as a full 9-section structure; this audit does not redefine those sections.
The observed issue is often record-boundary ambiguity, not simply missing filenames: an ID can appear in a batch or mixed report without a separately validated instance.
A claimed lifecycle status in a report is not equivalent to owner adjudication or independent review.
Phase 28 and Phase 30 already record these candidates as unverified; Phase 34 preserves rather than overwrites that state.
release_conditions: Locate and inspect the authoritative source-record contract and ERS-001 definition before declaring field-level conformance.
Record owner decisions in Phase 33 gate with owner identity, date, rationale, and evidence references.
Only then update proposed CIR/EIR drafts and validate them in a separate migration PR.
